refutation_attempt: Searched every path that could add a MatrixTransform parameter (Effect ctor, SpriteEffect, renderers) and found none, so the null cache holds. Then checked the XNA IL and spec: XNA 4.0 has no public SpriteEffect, so the entry's XNA-parity premise is false.
reason: The dead OnApply body contradicts CNA's own class and OnApply Doxygen, so it is a real low bug. The claim that XNA 4.0's SpriteEffect carries MatrixTransform is wrong: XNA 4.0 has no public SpriteEffect; its SpriteBatch owns a private Effect and sets MatrixTransform itself.

correction.expected: CNA's own SpriteEffect header documents the class as applying "a single world-view-projection matrix transform to a textured quad" and its OnApply() as applying "the sprite transform matrix parameter to the graphics device". OnApply() in SpriteEffect.cpp computes exactly that (Matrix::CreateOrthographicOffCenter over the viewport, multiplied after Matrix::CreateTranslation(-0.5f, -0.5f, 0.0f)). Note on XNA: XNA 4.0 has no public SpriteEffect type; its SpriteBatch owns a private Effect built from an embedded SpriteEffectCode blob and sets that effect's MatrixTransform parameter itself in PrepRenderState. A public SpriteEffect with a MatrixTransform parameter that Apply() fills is therefore a CNA class, not an XNA 4.0 contract.
correction.actual: Both constructors call SpriteEffect::CacheEffectParameters(), which stores getParametersProperty()["MatrixTransform"]. Nothing ever adds a parameter of that name: Effect::Effect(GraphicsDevice&) adds only a technique named Default, and SpriteEffect adds no parameter. EffectParameterCollection::operator[](const std::string&) returns nullptr for an absent name, so matrixParam_ is always null and OnApply() returns at its first statement. Code that reads effect.getParametersProperty()["MatrixTransform"] on a SpriteEffect receives a null pointer, and Apply() never computes the projection its own documentation describes.

refutation_attempt: Looked for a compensating registration (Texture base copy ctor, ContentManager cache, renderer registry) and a test pinning copy semantics; found none. Found that Texture::Dispose never checks the device lifetime token, contradicting the entry's claim that every device call is gated.
reason: Copies stay unregistered and undisposed after GraphicsDevice::Dispose, and a cross-device copy assignment leaves a dangling registry entry; both re-derived. Correction: Texture::Dispose calls into its device without the lifetime token, so an unregistered copy outliving the device touches a destroyed device, which the entry denied.

correction.actual:
Fixed since the finding was first recorded: moves. GraphicsResource(GraphicsResource&&) and operator=(GraphicsResource&&) call GraphicsDevice::TransferResourceReference, texture moves also call TransferMovedTexture, and the GraphicsResource-level device calls are gated on the weak graphicsDeviceLifetime_ token, so a moved-from address no longer stays in the registry and GraphicsResource::Dispose(bool) no longer calls into a destroyed device.
Still present: copies. GraphicsResource(const GraphicsResource&) copies the device pointer, the lifetime token, name and tag but never calls AddResourceReference. Texture2D and TextureCube default their copy operations, so the copy also shares the original's std::shared_ptr<ITextureRenderer>. Consequences, all by reading:
GetTrackedResourceCount() does not count the copy, and GraphicsDevice::Dispose() disposes only the registered original. The copy keeps reporting getIsDisposedProperty() == false and keeps the renderer texture alive; the allocation is released when the last copy dies, which can be after the renderer and its native context are gone (for example a static or global Texture2D destroyed at process exit). Whether that late release is harmless is backend- and driver-specific: EasyGLTextureRenderer's destructor, for instance, still deletes its GL name through its texture member once its registry has expired.
A copy that outlives its device also reaches Texture::Dispose (through Texture2D::Dispose or TextureCube::Dispose) with isDisposed_ still false, and Texture::Dispose calls RemoveDisposedTexture on graphicsDevice_->getTexturesProperty() and getVertexTexturesProperty() without checking the lifetime token, so it reads (and, if a slot still names the texture, writes) the storage of a GraphicsDevice that no longer exists. Registered originals do not reach that call, because GraphicsDevice::Dispose() has already marked them disposed.
GraphicsResource::operator=(const GraphicsResource&) re-points graphicsDevice_ without removing the wrapper from its old device or adding it to the new one. A Texture2D constructed on device A and then copy-assigned from a texture of device B stays in A's registry; if it is destroyed first, its Dispose(false) unregisters from B (a no-op) and leaves a dangling pointer in A's registry, which A.Dispose() later calls Dispose() through.
These copies are routine, not exotic: ContentManager::Load<T> stores a copy of every loaded Texture2D in its std::any cache and returns a further copy on every cache hit, so only the wrapper returned by the first load of an asset is registered.

refutation_attempt: Checked whether HEADLESS documents the always-1 answer as a deliberate contract or overrides the flags elsewhere; the header comment covers only PixelCount, while SupportsCapability's default arm and the interface default (true) both survive. The capability test pins true via its catch-all.
reason: HeadlessRenderer::SupportsCapability falls to true for OcclusionQuery and the interface PixelCountIsPreciseEXT default is true, yet PixelCount is the constant 1; this contradicts GraphicsCapability::OcclusionQuery's 'real raster-sample' doc and the truthful-override comment. Narrow, HEADLESS-only, low severity.

refutation_attempt: Traced Present() and the diff: Present() snapshots the running totals and the getter subtracts that snapshot, so it returns zeros right after a Present. Checked whether docs or plan define it as current-frame; the plan and test do, but the in-repo header comment says otherwise.
reason: HeadlessRenderer::GetLastFrameStatistics returns running counters minus the snapshot of the latest Present, i.e. the frame in progress; the header comment promises the frame ending at that Present. The test and plan pin current-frame semantics, so the stale comment and name are the defect; comment lives in the repo, so it counts as a bug.

refutation_attempt: Looked for a driver-format guard or shadercross fallback on the compute and ShaderEffect SPIR-V routes and for a device-level override of the capability. Only the stock-shader route has the shadercross fallback; the device-level answer is exactly the renderer's device_ != nullptr.
reason: Re-derived: GraphicsDevice::SupportsCapability(ComputeShaders) forwards to SupportsComputeShadersEXT (device_ != nullptr), and both compute and ShaderEffect SPIR-V intakes create SPIR-V-format objects with no shadercross route. Failure on D3D12/Metal drivers rests on CNA's own build comments, not on a run.

refutation_attempt: Searched for any unlatch or reset on the constructor's catch path and for a copied-state early return that would make the four post-resolution pushes no-ops. Only ResetForTestingEXT unlatches, and BlendState's copy takes a fresh state_, so the pushes do reach the renderer.
reason: resolveRenderer latches as its last step; the constructor then runs viewport and three state pushes inside try, and the catch destroys the renderer without unlatching. The design comment (RTR-P5-18) says a throwing construction must not freeze the selection. Real but narrow; not the IsLatched documentation defect (215/219/226).

refutation_attempt: Looked for a cleanup path: try/catch or scope guard in the constructor, an RAII wrapper for instance_/debugMessenger_/device_, and a factory that cleans up after a throw. None exists; the factory is a bare make_unique, and PickPhysicalDevice throws after the instance and surface exist.
reason: VulkanRenderer's constructor creates raw handles in sequence with no cleanup; the destructor cannot run for a throwing constructor, so instance_ (plus debug messenger, device, swapchain on later throws) leaks. The two PickPhysicalDevice refusals are routine on GPU-less hosts. Low impact, accurately scoped.

refutation_attempt: Checked whether RenderTargetPool, the passes or the chain compensate (a DeviceReset subscription, a shared pool, a reset entry on the fog pass) and whether the pipeline's own pool covers pass targets. None does; the cited tests pass only because the estimate omits the private pools.
reason: releaseDeviceResourcesEXT resets only sceneTarget_ and chain_'s pool; BloomPass, SsaoPass and VolumetricFogPass keep private RenderTargetPool members that neither the reset nor the estimate touches, contradicting 'drops every target the pipeline owns'. Real harm after a loss is renderer-dependent, so low is right.

refutation_attempt: Looked for a scope guard, try/catch or no-throw rule on the callbacks; begin() and end() have none and the header is silent. Traced both throw paths: frameOpen_ stays true and the shadow pass and order-independent accumulation stay open. Tests throw only from user passes.
reason: RenderPipeline::begin raises frameOpen_ then runs ShadowMap::begin, the caster callback and end unguarded; end lowers it and runs the transparent callback before unbinding. The contract is the in-repo MOD-713/MOD-1697 exception-safety principle, not a header guarantee. Real, low severity; 'unrecoverable' holds for shadows and order-independent transparency.

refutation_attempt: Searched all plan and remediation records for later runs, fixes or causes for the 24 tests. Counts match STREETS-0008, but two causes are recorded (a double free; a stale depth-clear test), so 'no cause recorded' is false. Nothing was re-run, so 'reproduced' is wrong.
reason: The 26-failure record (PSG-0009 to STREETS-0008) is real and is the newest before TARGET. But SMG-0041 records a double free for ConstructorExceptionSafety and GTI-0010 a stale depth-clear for BackbufferFormat, so 'no cause recorded' is false; and evidence is recorded-by-cna, since nothing was re-run.

correction.title: 24 classic SDL_GPU CTests still fail in CNA's latest recorded run; CNA's records name a cause for only three of them
correction.summary: CNA's SDL_GPU records list 26 classic ^SdlGpu CTests still failing just before TARGET; two are analysed in their own entries. Of the other 24, covering formats, render targets, render state and recovery, the records give a cause for two (a test that clears depth on a DepthFormat::None device, and a double free in the constructor failure path), a guess for a third, and nothing for the other 21.
correction.actual:
PSG-0009 (plans/plan_pre_sdlgpu_closeout.md) recorded 202 passing and 27 failing of 229 classic SDL_GPU CTests. The SDL_GPU modern-graphics and street workstreams re-ran the set after their changes and report "the same 27 by name" (SMG-0042: 204 / 27 of 231 with two new tests) until STREETS-0007 repaired SdlGpu_Smoke's stale checks; the last record before TARGET (STREETS-0008, plans/plan_street_sdlgpu.md) is 26 failures, "none new". Two of the 26 are analysed elsewhere (SdlGpu_OcclusionQuery_Limitation under CNA-BUG-012, SdlGpu_2D_HeadlessDriver under CNA-BUG-203). The other 24, grouped here by name only:
Formats and targets: SdlGpu_Texture2D_FormatMatrix, SdlGpu_Texture2D_FormatMatrixFallback, SdlGpu_TextureCube_FormatMatrix, SdlGpu_TextureCube_FormatMatrixFallback, SdlGpu_Parity_compressed_cube, SdlGpu_Parity_compressed_cube_fallback, SdlGpu_RenderTargetCube_Formats, SdlGpu_RenderTargetCube_MsaaMip, SdlGpu_RenderTarget_SetData, SdlGpu_TextureFilterMipContract, SdlGpu_EasyGLOracle_surface_format_throws.
State and draws: SdlGpu_RenderState, SdlGpu_DepthBias, SdlGpu_Deferred_Scissor, SdlGpu_DrawLineTopology, SdlGpu_EasyGLOracle_depthstencilstate_stencil_twosided, SdlGpu_EasyGLOracle_draw_range_validation, SdlGpu_Parity_dual_texture_terms, SdlGpuIndexedDrawRangeTest.MutatingSourceBuffersAfterQueuingDoesNotChangeQueuedDraws, SdlGpuIndexedDrawRangeTest.RejectsIndexedRangesOutsideTheBoundBuffers.
Device, presentation and lifetime: SdlGpu_BackbufferFormat, SdlGpu_ConstructorExceptionSafety, SdlGpu_SwapchainRecovery, SdlGpu_DepthlessCube_SpriteBatchCompatibility.
CNA's records name a cause for only three of the 24. SdlGpu_BackbufferFormat: plans/plan_gpu_test_isolation.md (GTI-0010) records that the test clears depth on a DepthFormat::None device, which GraphicsDevice::Clear refuses under XNA's rule (a stale test expectation). SdlGpu_ConstructorExceptionSafety: plans/plan_sdlgpu_modern_graphics.md (SMG-0041 and its classic-debt backlog) records an abort with "free(): double free detected in tcache 2", identical on the unmodified renderer sources, and calls it a real bug rather than test debt. SdlGpu_Parity_dual_texture_terms: PSG-0009 only suggests it may be the XNA opaque-black null-texture rule. The other 21 have no recorded cause.
correction.evidence_note: CNA's own record executed the set, on one machine: tools/platform/run_gpu_tests_private.sh (private Weston and rootful Xwayland), an AMD Radeon 780M under RADV Mesa 25.0.7, SDL_gpu on its Vulkan driver, a Release build with CNA_SDL_GPU_SHADERCROSS=OFF and libshaderc present (PSG-0010). The record calls them "Real renderer results, none of them a dead test", and STREETS-0008 re-ran all 27 on a stashed baseline to show they predate its change. Nothing was re-run for this entry: the evidence is recorded by CNA, not reproduced here, and whether each failure is a renderer defect, a stale expectation or specific to that machine is not established. Earlier records were greener: remediation/REMEDIATION_INDEX.md (REMED-GFX-180, 2026-07-31) reports a fully green 102-test SDL_GPU shard, and SdlGpu_SwapchainRecovery passed 5/5 when SDLGPU-11 added it, so some of these are later regressions or environment-specific. No CI workflow runs any SDL_GPU test.

refutation_attempt: Confirmed OnDeviceLost is a userdata-less free function that only logs, and deviceLost_ and Lost are set only in the debug hook. Then looked for a contract requiring real-loss propagation: the interface callback is opt-in, and plans/plan_webgpu.md WEBGPU-182 records the driver-reported path as not done.
reason: Facts hold, but nothing promises WEBGPU raises DeviceLost for a real loss: deviceEventCallback is opt-in, the docs describe only debug-hook recovery, and WEBGPU-182 states the driver-reported path is not done. That is a documented incomplete feature on an Experimental renderer. Residual doc drift: the header says the callback 'stays wired'.
read: docs/webgpu-renderer.md::Device loss: what the pin actually does, device-loss gate

correction.title: WEBGPU does not propagate a real device loss: OnDeviceLost only logs, so DeviceLost, the device status and the draw gate react only to the debug hooks
correction.summary: WebGPURenderer sets its lost flag, closes CanBeginDrawEXT() and raises DeviceLost only inside DebugSimulateContextLoss; the callback registered for a real loss only writes to stderr. CNA's own plan (WEBGPU-182) records the driver-reported path as not done and unverified, so this is an incomplete feature rather than a broken contract.
correction.expected: XNA raises DeviceLost and reports GraphicsDeviceStatus::Lost when the device is lost, and DirectX 9, 11 and 12, Direct2D and Vulkan raise it from their real error paths through GraphicsRendererCreateArgs::deviceEventCallback. That channel is opt-in, though, and for WEBGPU nothing documented promises a real loss reaches it: docs/webgpu-renderer.md describes recovery through the debug hooks only, and plans/plan_webgpu.md WEBGPU-182 closes with 'what is NOT done is the driver-reported path'. The same document adds a WebGPU-specific rule: a lost device must be gated before the acquire, because wgpuSurfaceGetCurrentTexture on a surface whose device is lost panics inside wgpu-native and aborts the process, and CanBeginDrawEXT() returning false is what stands between a lost device and that abort.
correction.actual: RequestDeviceOnlyEXT (also reached through RequestAdapterAndDevice) registers the free function OnDeviceLost as deviceLostCallbackInfo.callback with no user data. OnDeviceLost prints "CNA WebGPU device lost (...)" to stderr and does nothing else; without a renderer pointer it cannot set deviceLost_, raise RendererDeviceEvent::Lost or close CanBeginDrawEXT() (which returns !deviceLost_). The only code that does those things is WebGPURenderer::DebugSimulateContextLoss, and the only recovery is DebugRestoreContext; both are debug hooks the renderer never calls itself. When a real loss reaches the callback, the game receives no DeviceLost, GraphicsDeviceStatus stays Normal, BeginDraw keeps returning true and the renderer continues its frame loop against the lost device; nothing rebuilds it. The header comment of DebugSimulateContextLoss says the callback 'stays wired for a real driver-reported loss', which overstates what the callback does.

refutation_attempt: Compared with XNA's decompiled Reset: XNA also raises DeviceResetting and throws without DeviceReset, so those symptoms are not divergences, but XNA commits its cached parameters only after the native reset succeeds. Checked that a later-stage throw is reachable: Direct2D's UpdatePresentationFormatEXT throws for non-Color formats.
reason: Stored parameters, adapter and virtual size stay changed when a renderer call after the rollback try throws, unlike XNA, which commits only on success. Corrected: unpaired DeviceResetting/DeviceReset and the unrefreshed viewport match XNA's failed Reset and are not defects; the REMED-GFX-029 comment covers only the resize stage.

correction.expected: XNA 4.0's GraphicsDevice.Reset (read from the decompiled IL) copies the new PresentationParameters into its cached and public parameter objects only after the native reset succeeded, so a failed Reset leaves the previous values reported; on failure XNA raises DeviceResetting and throws without raising DeviceReset. CNA's own REMED-GFX-029 comment states the same intent for the window and resize stage: "a renderer resize is a failed Reset, not a partially successful one", with all public presentation bookkeeping restored before the exception is rethrown.
correction.actual: In modules/graphics/src/Xna/GraphicsDevice.cpp only applyPresentationParametersToWindow() and SetVirtualResolution() are inside the rollback try. The following renderer calls - UpdatePresentationFormatEXT, ApplyMultiSampleCount and SetSwapInterval - run after presentationParameters_, adapter_, the virtual size and the touch-panel size were replaced and after any bound render targets were unbound. If one throws (Direct2D's UpdatePresentationFormatEXT, for example, throws NotSupportedException for any backbuffer format other than Color or depth format other than None), the exception escapes with the new values stored, so the device keeps reporting presentation parameters, adapter and virtual size that the renderer rejected. The missing DeviceReset after DeviceResetting and the unrefreshed viewport are what XNA's own failed Reset does; the divergence is the stored state.
correction.evidence_note: Checked by reading the named sources at 009d40f5 and XNA 4.0's decompiled GraphicsDevice.Reset; nothing was built or executed. The regression test should assert that PresentationParameters, adapter and virtual size are unchanged after a later-stage failure; it should not require DeviceReset to be raised, because XNA does not raise it.

refutation_attempt: Checked whether the D3D9 throws are deliberate: D9-11 made silent no-ops loud, but GraphicsDevice.hpp documents SetStringMarkerEXT as a no-op off Vulkan and plan_dx.md calls the no-op right for D3D11/12. The DX contract test excludes D3D9; no D3D9 test calls either hook.
reason: DirectX9Renderer overrides both hooks with NotYetImplemented (std::runtime_error) although GraphicsDevice::SetStringMarkerEXT is documented as a no-op off Vulkan, and GraphicsDevice::SetContextRecoveryEnabled stores contextRecoveryEnabled_ before forwarding, so a throw leaves the Texture2D shadow policy changed. Both halves re-derived.

refutation_attempt: Looked for a usage-aware MRT path: the proxy builds its pass with no usage input, RTPassKey has no usage field, and neither SplitRenderPassEXT nor the shared SetRenderTargets adds a load. XNA's IL restores preserved targets in a set. The MRT test never rebinds one.
reason: VulkanMRTProxy always uses GetOrCreateMRTRenderPass, whose colour and depth attachments are LOAD_OP_CLEAR from UNDEFINED unless a split continuation, and whose key has no usage flag, while single-target passes have separate discard and load variants. XNA's SetRenderTargets restores each PreserveContents target in an MRT set. Cosmetic: the single-target function is GetOrCreateRTRenderPass(colorFmt, depthFmt, discardContents, storeAll).

refutation_attempt: Searched the whole DX9 module for a SupportsCapability override, a derived-capability arm in GraphicsDevice, and any shared clamp of MaxAnisotropy; none exists. ApplySamplerState writes the raw value while the compiled-effect path clamps to caps.MaxAnisotropy. No DX9 test touches either.
reason: DirectX9Renderer has no SupportsCapability override, so AnisotropicFiltering and MultiSampleAntiAliasing take the interface default true although GraphicsCapability documents MSAA as 'any sample count above 1' and anisotropy as device-dependent. ApplySamplerState skips the clamp its own compiled-effect route applies. Real but low: only devices lacking the feature or with low caps.

refutation_attempt: Looked for a compensating layer: another SdlRenderer path reading ScissorTestEnable, a shared scissor reset when the test is off, or CPU clipping in the sprite batch. Only setScissorRectangleProperty calls SetScissorRect and the module has no other clip code. Not the CNA-BUG-113 zero-area defect.
reason: SdlRenderer::SetScissorRect sets SDL_SetRenderClipRect for any non-empty rectangle and clears it for an empty one, and SDL_RENDERER never overrides ApplyRasterizerState, so ScissorTestEnable has no effect. XNA clips only when the test is enabled. The stale-rectangle UI pattern makes this a plausible medium.

refutation_attempt: Enumerated every Effect::Clone override to test 'every stock effect refuses a disposed source'. ShaderEffect does clone a disposed source, but so do PbrEffect, SkinnedPbrEffect and ColorMatrixEffect: no explicit check, and their copy constructors call Effect(device), bypassing the checking Effect copy constructor.
reason: ShaderEffect::Clone builds a new ShaderEffect from retained sources with no disposed check, against the base Effect::Clone @throws ObjectDisposedException contract. The claim that ShaderEffect is the lone exception is wrong: three CNA extension effects share the hole. Widen the scope; the disposed-clone test covers BasicEffect only.
read: modules/graphics/src/Xna/BasicEffect.cpp, AlphaTestEffect.cpp, DualTextureEffect.cpp, EnvironmentMapEffect.cpp, SkinnedEffect.cpp, SpriteEffect.cpp::Clone

correction.title: ShaderEffect, PbrEffect, SkinnedPbrEffect and ColorMatrixEffect clone a disposed source instead of throwing ObjectDisposedException
correction.summary: The five XNA stock effects, SpriteEffect and the compiled Effect::Clone() refuse a disposed source since SOFTWARE-259, but ShaderEffect::Clone rebuilds from its retained source strings, and the CNA extension effects PbrEffect, SkinnedPbrEffect and ColorMatrixEffect copy-construct through Effect(device), so none of the four checks.
correction.expected: Effect::Clone()'s documented contract in modules/graphics/include/Microsoft/Xna/Framework/Graphics/Effect.hpp: "@throws System::ObjectDisposedException If this effect has been disposed", implemented by Effect::ThrowIfDisposedForCloneInternal and pinned for BasicEffect by StockEffectCloneConstructorTest.CloneOfADisposedEffectIsRefused.
correction.actual: modules/graphics/src/Xna/ShaderEffect.cpp's Clone is new ShaderEffect(*device_, vertSrc_, fragSrc_) plus three label copies, with no disposed check. PbrEffect::Clone, SkinnedPbrEffect::Clone and ColorMatrixEffect::Clone call their copy constructors, which initialise the base with Effect(*src.device_) rather than the Effect copy constructor that calls ThrowIfDisposedForCloneInternal, and add no check of their own; a disposed source is cloned silently.
correction.evidence_note: Checked by reading every Effect subclass's Clone and copy constructor at 009d40f5; nothing was built or executed. The disposed-clone test covers BasicEffect only.

refutation_attempt: Confirmed the 3D cascade never reads customEffectRenderer or customEffectRequested. Then tested the SpriteBatch under-claim: engine-layer passes gate on ExecutesShaderEffectSourceEXT and draw through 3D, so a true answer would over-promise there, and CNA calls a fixed path legitimate when false. That half fails.
reason: The 3D half stands: DrawPrimitivesExImpl ignores the custom effect, so 16-byte streams draw with BasicEffect and other strides throw a BasicEffect layout error, against GpuDrawParams' refuse-by-customEffectRequested protocol. The under-claim half is not a defect: the query is renderer-wide, PostProcessPass draws ShaderEffect as 3D, and true would be unsafe.

correction.title: DIRECTX9 draws a 3D ShaderEffect with the stock BasicEffect shader (16-byte vertices) or fails with a BasicEffect vertex-layout error instead of using or refusing the custom effect
correction.summary: DIRECTX9 compiles ShaderEffect HLSL and runs it for SpriteBatch, but its 3D dispatch never reads GpuDrawParams::customEffectRenderer or customEffectRequested, so a 3D ShaderEffect draw is drawn with the stock vertex-colour BasicEffect shader (16-byte vertices) or fails with a BasicEffect vertex-layout runtime_error that does not name the custom effect.
correction.expected: GpuDrawParams documents both fields: customEffectRenderer, when non-null, is what the renderer 'should bind/draw with ... directly instead of selecting one of its own built-in stride-dispatched shaders', and customEffectRequested is there so that 'backends without custom shaders ... refuse the draw instead of mistaking a null renderer for an ordinary fixed-function stock effect'. CNA also accepts a renderer that takes a ShaderEffect object and draws with a fixed path while ExecutesShaderEffectSourceEXT() answers false (SOFTWARE and HEADLESS), so within that contract a route that cannot run the custom program should use its fixed path consistently or refuse by name. DIRECTX11 and DIRECTX12 read customEffectRequested and run the source.
correction.actual: modules/renderers/directx9/src/DirectX9Renderer.cpp's CreateEffectRenderer compiles the caller's HLSL (SM2/SM3) into a D3D9EffectRenderer, and modules/renderers/directx9/src/D3D9SpriteBatch.cpp binds it for SpriteBatch, so there the source does determine the pixels. For 3D, ShaderEffect::FillGpuDrawParams sets only customEffectRequested and customEffectRenderer, which modules/renderers/directx9/src/D3D9EffectDraw.cpp's DrawPrimitivesExImpl never reads. With the remaining GpuDrawParams defaults (vertex colour on, texture and lighting off) the cascade reaches DrawBasicEffectEXT, which draws a 16-byte (VertexPositionColor) stream with the stock vertex-colour shader and throws std::runtime_error ("(BasicEffect): stride N ... has no matching CNA vertex layout") for every other stride. Neither outcome names the unsupported custom effect. DirectX9Renderer answers ExecutesShaderEffectSourceEXT() false; that answer is not part of this defect, because the query is renderer-wide and engine-layer passes such as PostProcessPass draw their ShaderEffect as 3D, where a true answer would over-promise.
correction.evidence_note: Checked by reading at 009d40f5; nothing was built or executed. The DIRECTX9 ShaderEffect work item (plans/plan_dx9.md, D9-112) scoped the feature to SpriteBatch::Begin(effect), so the missing 3D execution is a known scope limit; what remains is the silent stock-effect fallback and the misleadingly named failure. XNA games use compiled effects, which DIRECTX9 supports separately; ShaderEffect is a CNA extension.

refutation_attempt: Read the profile feature docs, the ShaderDialectEXT::SpirV doc, the SDL_GPU header and the Vulkan snapshot test. The six features are documented as source-based; SpirV is bytecode; SDL_GPU says GLSL is deliberately not claimed; the Vulkan test asserts the six-Unsupported answer agrees with dialect SpirV.
reason: The six Unsupported answers are intentional and pinned, not a mapping slip: the ShaderDialect* features mean source text, SpirV is documented as bytecode, and SDL_GPU deliberately does not claim libshaderc GLSL. What survives is a vocabulary gap: the profile has no entry for pre-compiled SPIR-V payloads, so callers must use SupportsShaderLanguageEXT.

correction.title: The renderer capability profile has no feature for pre-compiled SPIR-V payloads, so SDL_GPU and VULKAN report every source-dialect feature Unsupported
correction.summary: BuildRendererCapabilityProfileEXT maps a renderer's declared dialect onto six source-dialect features (desktop GLSL, GLSL ES, Vulkan GLSL, HLSL, MSL, WGSL). SDL_GPU and VULKAN declare SpirV, which CNA documents as already-compiled bytecode rather than source text, so all six read Unsupported by design and the profile has no entry that says a SPIR-V payload is accepted.
correction.expected: The RendererFeature ShaderDialect* entries are documented as 'Source-based effects consume ...', and ShaderDialectEXT::SpirV as 'Already-compiled SPIR-V bytecode, not Vulkan GLSL source text'. The profile exists so that a caller can choose a payload without trying it; for a bytecode-consuming renderer the machine-readable profile cannot say which payload it takes.
correction.actual: BuildRendererCapabilityProfileEXT in modules/graphics/src/Xna/GraphicsDevice.cpp sets ShaderDialectGlslDesktop/GlslEs/GlslVulkan/Hlsl/Msl/Wgsl to supported only when ExecutesShaderEffectSourceEXT() is true and the declared dialect equals that enumerator. SDL_GPU and VULKAN declare ShaderDialectEXT::SpirV, for which no feature exists, so all six read Unsupported. This is deliberate and pinned: vulkan_capability_snapshot_test.cpp asserts that dialect SpirV, source execution false and six Unsupported source dialects agree, and SdlGpuRenderer.hpp says GLSL is deliberately not claimed even in a libshaderc build, because that route compiles Vulkan-rule GLSL where the engine layer's GLSL ES is not a legal input. SDL_GPU answers ExecutesShaderEffectSourceEXT() true while VULKAN answers false, so the SDL_GPU profile shows source execution supported with no source dialect. A caller must ask GraphicsDevice::SupportsShaderLanguageEXT(SpirV, stage) instead.
correction.evidence_note: Checked by reading the named sources at 009d40f5; nothing was built or executed. No SDL_GPU profile snapshot exists.

refutation_attempt: Counted the enumerators (19) against the switch cases (18) and confirmed IndirectDraw is the gap, with no default and no -Wswitch. Then searched for a compensating test and found RequireCapabilityTest.EveryCapabilityHasItsOwnName, which the entry says does not exist; its hand-written list omits IndirectDraw too.
reason: nameOfCapability omits IndirectDraw and the 'fails to compile' comment is false, since C++ only warns and graphics-ext enables no -Wswitch. Corrected: a test does enumerate capabilities through nameOfCapability (EveryCapabilityHasItsOwnName), but its own hand-written list is missing IndirectDraw, so it cannot catch the omission.

correction.actual: modules/graphics-ext/src/RequireCapability.cpp lists 18 of the 19 members of CNA::GraphicsCapability (modules/graphics/include/CNA/GraphicsCapability.hpp) and omits IndirectDraw, falling through to "an unrecognised capability". A missing enumerator in a switch without default does not fail compilation in C++ (only -Wswitch warns, and neither graphics-ext nor the root CMake enables it), so the safeguard the comment relies on does not exist. At 009d40f5 the indirect-draw users (StorageBuffer.cpp, GpuInstanceCuller.cpp) test the capability directly, so no current refusal prints the wrong name.
